newsitem.title: UK: Copper ends near 2-1/2 mth high, seen higher still.
newsitem.headline: Copper ends near 2-1/2 mth high, seen higher still.

text.p: Copper prices charged higher during an extremely active Friday LME session, with prices hitting the highest for 2-1/2 months on waves of fund buying, shortcovering and option delta purchases, traders said.

The market rose in excess of five percent today, ranging from $2,010 to $2,152 before closing at $2,148 a tonne, a gain of $117 from Thursday. Declining warehouse inventories and widening backwardations induced the dramatic moves.
"Copper was the only game in town today - the others hardly moved in comparison. Everybody is a bit shell-shocked now," one trader said.
Traders said the market has largely discounted reports earlier this week of a large hidden stockpile and is focussing on dwindling visible stocks.

LME inventories fell by 8,000 tonnes to a new 6-1/4 year low of 101,175 tonnes. Confirmation of a decline kicked the market higher, with the lack of a sizeable tonnage delivered into Singapore also supportive.

There were 5,500 tonnes landed, but this much lower than the 20,000/40,000 tonnes that many recently expected to be registered. Some traders said this metal has already been snapped up, and will not be placed on warrant.

Option delta hedging kicked in as downside strikes receded and upside calls got closer to in-the-money. The option postions in December are sizeable, and further covering against these has the potential to drive the market much higher, they said.

Meanwhile, the cash/threes backwardation widened from $80/85 on Thursday to $105/115, and as sensitive December dates draw closer is likely to expand further. Three months prices are seen testing $2,165 soon, then moving up above $2,200, they said.
Elsewhere, the other metals took a back seat, with aluminium clawing its way towards $1,450 after a stock decline. Last trade was at $1,442, up $14.
Nickel prices fell throughout the session, initially responding to a 570-tonne stock increase, then on chart selling.
The market is now vulnerable to a challenge of the $7,000 level on the downside. Last kerb trade was at $7,050 a tonne, down $110 from Thursday.
The zinc market made gradual upward progress today, with momentum from copper enough to see prices residing above $1,060 by the end of the session.
News Spain's Asturiana had finally liquidated its LME futures position came as no surprise as this operation had been continuing for some time.
But with this large market position, which dates back to the early 1990s out of the way, there is more scope for longer-term upside movement. Last trade was at $1,064, up $4.50.
Lead's attempts to push higher faltered above $730, and by the end of the kerb the market was back at an unchanged $725.
Tin was supported by an inventory decline of 260 tonnes, with speculative buying lifting prices above $6,000. Last trade was at $6,060, up $80.
The alloy market was marked up with primary metal, and closed at a steadier $1,310/1,312.
